correctness.rationale: The original Jagiella Proposition 5.2 (full primary text, Section 5) reduces finite-dimensional omega-interpretation to dimension one with fixed finite defining parameters A. A dimension-one omega quotient has nonempty pairwise disjoint classes L_n; Jagiella Definition 2.9 explicitly states that every level is finite by minimality. Each n is definable without parameters in (omega,<) (using successor/number of predecessors), so its pullback L_n is A-definable and finite. Any member of any L_n lies in acl(A), including every original element because the dimension-one interpretation is over the whole M; alternatively any finite definable omitted part is algebraic. Locally finite acl would make M finite. No hypothesis on ambient ordered reduct needed beyond Jagiella general dimension-reduction proposition. The conclusion is about home sort, not imaginaries or all elementary-extension elements.
